title: Lake Lichtsee Obernberg am Brenner
name: Lake Lichtsee Obernberg am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Lichtsee at 2,101 m in the Obernbergtal: crystal-clear high-alpine lake with world-famous reflections of the mighty Obernberger Tribulaun.
beschreibung:
Overview

The magical Lichtsee perches at a high-alpine elevation of 2,101 meters nestled in a sunny glacial cirque within the Stubai Alps in the picturesque Obernbergtal – one of the most pristine side valleys of the Tyrolean Wipptal (Innsbruck-Land district). With its mirror-like, crystal-clear surface and untouched high-alpine flora, this natural moraine lake ranks among the most photogenic and awe-inspiring mountain tarns in the entire Eastern Alps. The lake is renowned for the spectacular water reflections of the striking rock massif of the Obernberger Tribulaun (2,780 m).

Alpine Natural Gem & Hiking Tour

The lake owes its name to the exceptionally clear, light-flooded water shimmering in multifaceted hues of blue and green. In early summer, the shores blossom with a vibrant sea of deep pink alpine roses, white cotton grass, and gentians. Despite the extreme elevation and chilly water temperatures, the lake harbors a rare population of arctic char. The ascent to the lake is considered a classic Tyrolean mountain hike: from the valley hamlet of Obernberg, a scenic mountain footpath winds through shady larch and Swiss stone pine forests up to the expansive alpine meadows of the Kastnerbergalm and onward to the lake basin (walking time approx. 2.5 hours, climbing around 700 meters of elevation). The lakeshore commands a magnificent downward vista across the entire Obernbergtal and the glaciated Zillertal Alps.

Visit & Getting There

Lichtsee is open and freely accessible during the snow-free summer months from mid-June to mid-October (in late autumn and winter it is inaccessible or only reachable by experienced ski tourers, depending on snow conditions). Getting there by car: Via the Brenner motorway A13 (exit Nösslach) or the B182 to Gries am Brenner, branch off into the Obernbergtal and drive to the end of the valley at Obernberg am Brenner (paid hiking parking lot Waldesruh). By public transport: ÖBB S-Bahn to Steinach am Brenner or Gries am Brenner station, then continue with Postbus line 4145 directly to the Obernberg Waldesruh stop right at the trailhead.

Tips

The ascent to Lichtsee follows alpine trails and requires sturdy mountain boots with good tread as well as solid physical stamina. Pack plenty of drinking water and provisions, as there is no mountain hut catering directly at the lake. On your descent, a stop at the traditional Almgasthof Waldesruh is warmly recommended.
